paragraphs: Occupational scope | O*NET11-3051.02 manages the operation of geothermal power generation facilities and maintains and monitors equipment. Of the 18 tasks, 13 are core, 4 supplemental, and 1 new; employee safety training is New with importance NA and cannot be classified as supplemental or written as 0. Permit applications, compliance reporting, and grid interconnection negotiation are supplemental tasks; actual administrative approval and statutory inspection require separate checks. Wages and employment are a reference for parent occupation 11-3051 and cannot be treated as the geothermal occupation's own.

Fit signals | The work activity importance for U.S. O*NET 11-3051.02 shows: communicating with superiors, peers, or subordinates (92), organizing, planning, and prioritizing work (90), obtaining information (87), scheduling work and activities (86), using computers (86), making decisions and solving problems (85), building and developing teams (82), identifying objects, actions, and events (80), and monitoring processes, materials, or surroundings (80) are the most important activities for this occupation; the work context shows email 100% every day, telephone communication 100% every day, face-to-face or personal and team discussions 96% every day, working in a controlled indoor environment 96% every day, wearing routine protective or safety equipment 74% every day, and working in an enclosed vehicle or operating enclosed equipment 88% every day; work hours 90% more than 40 hours per week; responsibility for the health and safety of others 83% very high responsibility, and responsibility for the work results and outcomes of other workers 78% very high responsibility. If you are willing to coordinate continuously between field equipment and the control room screen, crews and contractors, and operations and maintenance, can judge priorities from parameters and alarm information and explain them clearly, and are glad to take responsibility for personnel safety and production results, the daily demands of this occupation are closer to how you work.

Caution signals | O*NET also shows (11-3051.02, percentage response measure): consequences of error 68% extremely serious; importance of being exact or highly accurate 48% extremely important; responsibility for the health and safety of others 83% very high responsibility; work hours 90% more than 40 hours per week; outdoor exposure to all weather 62% once a week or more but not every day; exposure to hazardous conditions 27% every day, exposure to contaminants 23% every day, and exposure to hazardous equipment 47% once a week or more but not every day; exposure to distracting or uncomfortable noise 59% once a week or more but not every day; work schedule 38% irregular (varying with weather, generation demand, or contract period); dealing with unpleasant, angry, or discourteous people 32% once a month or more but not every week; and conflict situations 50% once a week or more but not every day. This occupation deals with generating units, well fields and reinjection systems, electrical and control systems, and permitting and compliance, and a single unhandled parameter excursion, unconfirmed work permit or energy isolation, unrecorded corrosion or scaling or equipment anomaly, or mishandled permit condition or environmental report can affect equipment safety, personnel safety, and generation availability, and may also involve electric power work safety, special equipment, environmental protection, and occupational health management rules. If you find it hard to face the target position's actual shift and on-call conditions and noise, contaminants, and hazardous equipment over the long term, find it hard to accept serious consequences of error and a wide scope of responsibility, or are unwilling to take responsibility for personnel safety and the traceability of compliance records and equipment status, you should treat these as real costs that need careful weighing.

Taking responsibility | First check the power, permit conditions, missing records, versions, and budget in the G1 fictional materials, keep the first answers and the real corrections, and use the results to identify the skills and task preferences that need further practice. A single desktop item only shows this round's calculation and recording performance and cannot prove long-term field fit, independent command, or hazardous work qualifications; subsequent verification follows real training, mentoring, and target-position conditions.

Insufficient evidence: this round did not obtain a Chinese national occupational wage distribution or employment projection for geothermal production managers, and the National Bureau of Statistics industry and five job category aggregates cannot be filled in as substitutes; no claim is made on that basis that no other national data exists. Direct answer | 'Geothermal Production Managers' on this page is the exact occupation O*NET 11-3051.02 (Geothermal Production Managers), and its work can be divided into several categories: (one) operations and condition management — supervise geothermal plant and well field operations, inform employees of plant conditions, monitor operations using programmable logic controllers, and handle alarms and condition changes according to operating procedures; (two) maintenance and repair — perform or direct preventive maintenance of geothermal plant equipment, inspect the geothermal plant and reinjection well field to verify equipment operation, and troubleshoot and carry out minor repairs on instrumentation or electrical systems; (three) equipment and system improvement — identify and evaluate inefficiencies in equipment, procedures, or conditions, identify opportunities to improve electrical equipment, control, or process control methods, and select and implement corrosion control or mitigation systems; (four) well field and resource-side management — carry out well field site assessments, focusing on reinjection and well field equipment condition; (five) planning, budget, and compliance — develop geothermal operating plans and schedules, prepare or manage operating budgets, prepare environmental permit applications or compliance reports, obtain construction, upgrade, or operating permits, and negotiate interconnection agreements with other utilities; (six) personnel and safety — supervise employees, build and develop teams, and conduct employee safety training; (seven) records and information — record, review, or maintain daily logs, reports, and maintenance records. Work cycle linkage: operating plan and scheduling — shift operation, control room monitoring, and condition communication — preventive maintenance and repair — anomaly and inefficiency identification and correction — permitting, compliance, and interconnection matters — records and review. This page does not conflate this occupation with the adjacent industrial production managers, quality control systems managers, biofuel production managers, biomass power plant managers, or hydroelectric production managers, nor does it expand the duties of an operations management position into replacing engineering design, statutory equipment inspection, or interconnection and permit approval.

Occupational highlights | O*NET11-3051.02 tasks include supervising employees and operations and maintenance 84, condition communication 77, inefficiency identification and preventive maintenance 75, inspecting the reinjection well field 74, budget and corrosion control 73, planning 72, logs 71, PLC and well field assessment 69, and control improvement 67. There are also 4 supplemental tasks and 1 new safety training task (NA); New differs from Supplemental. Wages are parent occupation 2025, the current projection is BLS direct 2025—2035, and no claim is made that O*NET has already synchronized.

Boundary conclusion | This page corresponds to O*NET 11-3051.02 (Geothermal Production Managers), and the core difference from adjacent positions lies in 'object, output, and actual authorization': this occupation takes the operation and maintenance, compliance, and personnel safety of in-service geothermal generating units as its object, produces operating, maintenance, permit, interconnection, budget, and record results, and is directly responsible for on-site personnel safety and generation availability; Industrial Production Managers (11-3051.00) take the output, cost, quality, and personnel management of manufacturing production systems as their object and produce production plans and performance; Quality Control Systems Managers (11-3051.01) take quality systems, inspection, and auditing as their object and produce quality system and audit conclusions; Biofuel Production Managers (11-3051.03), Biomass Power Plant Managers (11-3051.04), and Hydroelectric Production Managers (11-3051.06) respectively take their own feedstock and conversion processes or hydraulic works and units as their object and produce the operating and compliance results of their own processes and units. Objects and processes differ, and authorization is checked against the actual activities, jurisdiction, and institution, so authority for interconnection negotiation, permit applications, or special equipment inspection cannot be carried over from one position to another.

Core idea of adjacent positions | Most positions in the same group and adjacent positions aim to 'keep a production, quality, or engineering system running stably and continuously improving within the boundaries of authorization, safety, and compliance', and the differences lie in the object, output, and actual authorization: some take in-service geothermal generating units and well fields as their object, some take manufacturing production systems, some take quality systems and inspection, and some take a specific fuel or hydraulic process.

Core purpose of this occupation | Taking the operation and maintenance of in-service geothermal generating units and the well field, reinjection, electrical and control systems, compliance, and personnel safety as its object, complete management and coordination work within operating procedures and the boundaries of safety, permits, and authorization: organize shift operation and control room monitoring, direct preventive maintenance and repair, identify and handle inefficiencies, corrosion, and anomalies, and handle permit, interconnection, and budget matters, so that generation runs efficiently and safely, equipment status and compliance records are traceable, and boundaries can be explained.

Main objects and basis of adjacent positions | Industrial production managers rely on manufacturing process, production planning, cost, and quality management methods; quality control systems managers rely on quality system standards and inspection and audit methods; biofuel production managers, biomass power plant managers, and hydroelectric production managers rely on their own fuel or hydraulic processes and unit and permit methods; energy engineers rely on energy system design and energy efficiency evaluation methods.

Main objects and basis of this occupation | The objects are geothermal generating units and well fields and reinjection systems, electrical and control and protection devices, pressure and special equipment, corrosion and scaling control, environmental permits and interconnection agreements, and operation, maintenance, and safety records; the basis is operating procedures and manufacturer requirements and electric power work safety, special equipment, environmental protection, occupational health, and permit requirements, along with institutional safety and quality rules.

Geothermal Production Managers manage the operation, maintenance, monitoring, and personnel of geothermal power generation facilities, producing operating plans, maintenance and corrosion control arrangements, budgets, logs, and permit applications and compliance materials. Plant Manager and similar are O*NET reported titles, and uniform authority is not inferred from the title. The parent occupation's 73% in manufacturing is the 2024 industrial production manager distribution and cannot be used to judge geothermal power employers; the highest work activities are communication 92, organizing and planning 90, and obtaining information 87.
This round the 2025 parent occupation industrial production managers show 74% in manufacturing, which is not a geothermal employer distribution, and the older 2024 figure of 73% is historical only.

Core process of adjacent positions | Industrial production managers focus on production planning, scheduling, work orders, cost, and personnel management; quality control systems managers focus on quality systems, inspection, sampling, audits, and corrective actions; biofuel production managers, biomass power plant managers, and hydroelectric production managers focus on their own feedstock or hydraulic works and unit operation, maintenance, and permits; energy engineers focus on scheme design, calculation, energy efficiency accounting, and technical renovation.

Core process of this occupation | Operating plan and scheduling, shift operation and control room monitoring and condition communication, preventive maintenance and repair, anomaly and inefficiency and corrosion identification and correction, permit, compliance, interconnection, and budget matters, and records, review, and archiving; every step must be documented according to the safety, quality, and permit rules and be reviewable by supervisors, dispatch, and regulators.

Main outputs of adjacent positions | Industrial production managers produce production plans, output, cost, and performance results; quality control systems managers produce quality system documents and inspection, audit, and corrective action records; biofuel production managers, biomass power plant managers, and hydroelectric production managers produce the operating, maintenance, and compliance results of their own processes or units; energy engineers produce design or renovation schemes and energy efficiency accounting results.

Main outputs of this occupation | Stable generation operation and condition records, preventive maintenance and repair and troubleshooting records, corrosion control and inefficiency correction records, environmental and operating permits and interconnection and budget and scheduling documents, employee safety training records, and traceable operating logs and alarm, verification, permit, and training records.

Responsible parties for adjacent positions | Responsibility for positions in the same group and adjacent positions is usually defined by the institution, specifications, and authorization, and the objects of responsibility are mostly production safety, product quality, the environment, and the public interest.

Responsible party for this occupation | Managers may, within their duties, organize operation and maintenance, repair, budgets, and permit applications and interconnection negotiations, and are responsible for their own judgments, direction, and the truthfulness of materials. Field work authorization follows the real rules, and government approval, statutory inspection, and prescribed engineering qualifications require separate checks; all permit, interconnection, or repair duties cannot be excluded from this occupation across the board.

Authority and approval of adjacent positions | The authority of positions in the same group and adjacent positions comes from institutional authorization, practice or qualification requirements, specifications, and rules, and usually does not include the authority to decide on its own conclusions, signatures, or data provision beyond its own authorization or scope; matters involving engineering, permits, inspection, compliance, and personal information should be referred to the corresponding position or institution.

Authority and approval of this occupation | Operating, maintenance, well field work, and energy isolation must take place within work permits and the authorized scope; putting alarm and protection devices in and out of service and bypassing them require approval according to the procedure; external submission of environmental and operating permits, interconnection, budgets, and maintenance plans must take place within institutional authorization and compliance requirements; matters involving statutory inspection of pressure or special equipment, interconnection agreement terms, major repairs or technical renovation schemes, and environmental protection and occupational health must obtain approval from or be referred to the corresponding position or institution according to the rules, and unauthorized operation or release is prohibited.

Conclusion boundaries of adjacent positions | Conclusions from positions in the same group and adjacent positions are mostly limited to this project, this process, and this duty level, and usually do not constitute a determination of equipment safety, compliance, or legal liability; cross-disciplinary conclusions and those involving permits, inspection, or legal use have limits on their applicability.

Conclusion boundaries of this occupation | Operating conclusions state only verifiable parameters, equipment status, and maintenance, verification, permit, and handling records, and distinguish field observation facts from judgment and inference and pending verification; unauthorized judgments and commitments must not be made on matters beyond one's authorization (engineering design, statutory inspection of pressure and special equipment, interconnection agreement terms, and environmental permits and major repair schemes); when parameters exceed limits, equipment anomalies occur, corrosion exceeds limits, records do not match the site, or permits are not met, work must be suspended and escalated or referred, and conclusions must also withstand review by superiors, dispatch, regulators, and accident investigations.

Pre-entry checking statement | The following six items are used to check item by item before applying and starting the job, to avoid inferring actual duties and authorization from the job title or promotional language; the checking results should be based on written recruitment information, the employment contract, position descriptions, and safety, quality, and permit rules and documents, and should be continuously confirmed after starting. This page lists checking directions only and does not constitute a formal conditions list for any institution or project. Special note: this occupation often involves pressure, energized, and rotating equipment, well field and reinjection work, work permits, energy isolation, and environmental protection and occupational health requirements, so be sure to confirm the position's specific requirements for safety training, protective equipment, work permits, certificate requirements, and data disclosure.

Notes on checking points | Position titles are similar but duties and authorization differ greatly: some focus on control room operation, monitoring, and dispatch, some on field maintenance, repair, and troubleshooting, some on well field, reinjection, and resource-side management, some on compliance, permits, and interconnection matters, and some on technical renovation and energy efficiency improvement; different institutions and jurisdictions also differ in the authorization for operating pressure and energized equipment, work permits, permit applications and interconnection negotiation, and data disclosure and external release.

Preface | The comparison below is organized in four columns: 'occupational direction — core work and outputs — key difference — what it is better suited to'. Geothermal, hydroelectric, and biomass generation, power plant operation, and geothermal technology are often linked within the same generation group or project, but linkage does not mean they are interchangeable; when choosing across directions, the process, procedures, permits, and responsibility boundaries of that direction must be learned anew.

Key difference: this occupation takes in-service geothermal generating units and the well field and reinjection as its object, organizing shift operation and control room monitoring, directing preventive maintenance and repair, identifying and handling inefficiencies and corrosion and anomalies, and handling permit, interconnection, and budget matters, and is responsible for on-site personnel safety and generation availability; the other positions respectively center on manufacturing production systems, hydraulic works and hydro units, biomass fuel and boiler and turbine processes, operating and monitoring according to procedures, and field testing and maintenance, and each usually has more specialized process, procedure, and authorization requirements and does not bear primary responsibility for geothermal unit operation or geothermal permit and interconnection matters (but must collaborate with operations management positions and define boundaries clearly).

Better suited to people who are willing to move between the control room and field equipment, can organize crews and contractors to complete operation and maintenance according to procedures, judge priorities from parameters and alarm information, explain anomalies and inefficiencies clearly and implement corrections, and are willing to take responsibility for on-site personnel safety and compliance records.

Core work and outputs: supervise geothermal plant or well field employees, organize shift operation and control room monitoring and inform employees of conditions, monitor operations using programmable logic controllers, perform or direct preventive maintenance and repair, carry out well field site assessments and corrosion control, handle environmental and operating permits and negotiate interconnection agreements, prepare operating budgets and schedules, and maintain operation and maintenance records; outputs are operating, maintenance, permit, interconnection, budget, and record results (O*NET/SOC 11-3051.02).

Responsibility preface | Efficiency can be outsourced to tools, but field judgment, safety, compliance, and personnel responsibility cannot. The five steps below are the human responsibility points that must be preserved before and after adopting any digital tool.

Needs and boundaries: operation and maintenance objectives, safety boundaries, and permit conditions must be determined by personnel with the corresponding authorization, and tools do not replace field judgment and plan and work permit judgment.

Field confirmation and quality: confirming equipment and well field and reinjection status, work permits, energy isolation, lockout and tagout, and instrument verification must be completed by the individual according to procedures, and tools do not replace field verification.

Data and judgment: parameter and alarm trends and analysis results must be checked and reviewed by the individual, tool output must not be used directly as the basis for operations, shutdown, putting equipment in or out of service, or reports, and judgments must not exceed the procedures and what the data supports.

Safety, compliance, and data: pressure, energized, height, confined space, and well field work and controlled data or data involving trade secrets or personal information must be managed according to minimum necessity and permit and retention period requirements, and tools must not be used to send them externally or generate unverified content.

Disclosure and change: permits, interconnection, external disclosure, and process and technical renovation changes must take place within the scope of authorization and safety and compliance requirements, and parameter excursions, equipment anomalies, or records that do not match the site must be reported according to the rules.

paragraphs: The following are editorial risk scenarios compiled from actual tasks, and no accident rate or failure frequency was obtained. Permit materials and interconnection negotiation are tasks this occupation may be involved in, while government approval and statutory inspection carry separate authority; engineering and equipment responsibility is checked against actual qualifications and authorization and cannot be excluded by the manager title.

Direct answer | The core risk in this occupation is not 'whether power can be generated' but four types of consequential failure: operation and equipment failure (parameter excursions, arbitrary locking out or bypassing of protection devices, unhandled corrosion and scaling and well field reinjection anomalies, and unverified instrumentation and control, which can damage equipment and affect generation availability), safety and environmental failure (unconfirmed work permits and energy isolation, pressure, energized, height, confined space, and well field work not carried out according to permits and protection, and improper disposal of contaminants, thermal discharge, and waste, which can cause personal and environmental accidents), record and compliance failure (missing operating logs, alarms, maintenance, verification, and training records or changes without a trace, non-conforming or overdue permit and interconnection conditions, and improper handling and disclosure of controlled or trade-secret data), and authorization and collaboration failure (exceeding authorization to replace engineers or inspection bodies in pressure and special equipment conclusions or interconnection and permit approval, key personnel or spare parts or outsourcing resting on a single point, and unclear permit, interconnection, and outsourcing delivery and acceptance causing interruption or disputes). Consequences of error 68% extremely serious, and responsibility for the health and safety of others 83% very high responsibility, are the work context basis for this occupation's consequential risk.

Context basis: consequences of error 68% extremely serious, safety of others 83% very high responsibility, more than 40 hours 90%, hazardous conditions 27% every day, and hazardous equipment 47% once a week but not every day, all O*NET answer categories rather than accident probabilities. China actual activity boundaries: in mainland China, requirements are checked against the actual activities: Article 28 of the Work Safety Law on education and training, and Article 30 on the designated special operations qualifications; Articles 2/14/39—42 of the Special Equipment Safety Law are checked against the inventory, personnel positions, and inspection and abnormal-status conditions, and not all managers hold one uniform certificate. Articles 18—22 of the Electric Power Law cover safety, maintenance, unified dispatch, and interconnection agreements; managers may prepare materials and negotiate within authorization but do not replace administrative approval or statutory inspection. The Ecological Environment Code takes effect on 2026-08-15 and repeals ten laws including the Environmental Protection Law, and obligations are checked against the project, emissions, and permit scope. Articles 34/35 of the Occupational Disease Prevention and Control Law check training and health examinations against occupational hazard exposure.

Parameter excursions or arbitrary locking out or bypassing of protection devices, or corrosion and scaling and well field reinjection anomalies not handled according to procedures, or unverified instrumentation and control; can damage units and equipment and affect generation availability and grid safety

Handle parameters and anomalies according to operating procedures and alarm levels, put protection devices in and out of service and bypass them only with procedural approval and documentation, verify instrumentation and control on schedule, and immediately isolate, review, and report any anomaly found; operating handling and verification results must be documented and traceable together with the log

Scenario | An alarm indicates a parameter excursion on a unit, the maintenance window is close, the parties want to bypass the protection device first to keep generating and explain later, and the approval and documentation have not been implemented.
The individual and maintenance and safety positions; workers, equipment, and contractors

Unconfirmed work permits, energy isolation, and lockout and tagout, or pressure, energized, height, confined space, and well field work not carried out according to permits and protection; can cause personal injury and equipment damage and safety incidents

Before work, complete the work permit, risk assessment, energy isolation, and lockout and tagout and confirm personnel qualifications and protective equipment; pressure, energized, and special equipment work is carried out according to procedures and certificate requirements, and working with hidden hazards is prohibited; stop and report immediately when permits or protection are inadequate

Scenario | During handover, the previous shift's work permit and energy isolation records are found to be incomplete, and contractors are still working near energized or pressurized equipment on site, and it is suggested to fill them in from a template and sign later.
The individual and operations and compliance positions; the institution, regulators, and grid enterprises

Missing operating logs, alarms, maintenance, verification, and training records or changes without a trace, or permit and interconnection conditions that do not conform or are not fulfilled on time; can violate electric power work safety and special equipment and environmental and permit requirements and affect compliance and accident tracing

Truthfully register conditions, alarms, repairs, and permit information; lawful corrections keep the original value, the true correction time, the reason, the basis, and the review, and backdating, falsification, traceless overwriting, or turning a missing item into a confirmed one is prohibited.

Scenario | To meet a compliance deadline, a person is asked to use unverified operating and emissions data in permit or interconnection materials and to send controlled or trade-secret data to unauthorized channels.
The individual and equipment and compliance positions; engineering and inspection and regulatory conclusions

Treating operating results or tool output as confirmed conclusions to replace engineering design or statutory inspection of pressure and special equipment or interconnection and permit approval; can cause wrong judgments and safety or compliance consequences

Operating and equipment conclusions must note the procedural basis and field status and limitations, and engineering design or statutory inspection or interconnection and permit approval is referred to the corresponding position or institution; when faced with overreach or conclusive demands, explain the boundaries first and refer according to the process

Scenario | With staff stretched thin, a person is asked to read directly from an unverified instrument, or to bypass procedures and state a conclusion on pressure equipment safety and interconnection conditions in the report so it can be submitted the same day.
The individual, the crew, and equipment positions; generation continuity and maintenance windows

Key operating experience, spare parts, instrumentation and control, outsourced maintenance, or certified personnel resting on a single point, so that operation and maintenance are interrupted during leave, resignation, equipment failure, or spare parts shortage; can delay maintenance and affect generation continuity and safety redundancy

Establish backup and handover rules for operating experience, spare parts, access rights, documents, certified personnel, and outsourced resources, and make key maintenance and test plans and parameters reproducible and documented; when staff, spare parts, or resources are insufficient, report according to procedures and adjust priorities, and do not operate with hidden hazards
Scenario | The only engineer familiar with a unit control system and maintenance process is on leave, and key maintenance and testing are requested to be taken over temporarily by untrained staff.
The individual and outsourcing and partner parties; maintenance and permit and interconnection and safety responsibility

Unclear delivery, acceptance, responsibility, and fee changes for outsourced maintenance, testing, or spare parts supply, or unclear agency and signing authority for interconnection and permit matters; can lead to rework, fee disputes, and unclear safety responsibility and compliance ownership

Collaboration and outsourcing must clearly define scope, standards, acceptance, certificates, safety responsibility, and fee change rules and be documented, and deliverables must be reviewed and accepted; when delivery, acceptance, or ownership disputes arise, pause, review, and report

Scenario | An outsourcing unit completes maintenance or testing and requests settlement and release without submitting maintenance records and verification and test data, and the site is asked to sign first and supplement later.

entries.answer: The geothermal production managers on this page are the exact occupation O*NET 11-3051.02 (Geothermal Production Managers): manage operations at geothermal power generation facilities, maintain and monitor geothermal plant equipment for efficient and safe plant operations. Core tasks include supervising geothermal plant or well field employees (importance 84), supervising geothermal plant operations and maintenance and repair to ensure compliance (84), informing employees of plant conditions (77), identifying and evaluating inefficiencies in equipment and procedures and conditions (75), performing or directing preventive maintenance (75), inspecting the geothermal plant or reinjection well field (74), preparing or managing operating budgets (73), selecting and implementing corrosion control or mitigation systems (73), developing operating plans and schedules (72), recording and reviewing logs and reports (71), using programmable logic controllers to monitor operations (69), and carrying out well field site assessments (69); it also includes supplemental tasks such as preparing environmental permit applications or compliance reports (82), negotiating interconnection agreements (79), and obtaining permits (73). Common job titles include Plant Manager, Plant Supervisor, and Power Plant Operations Manager. The 73% manufacturing industry share is the 2024 parent occupation distribution and cannot be used to infer geothermal employers.

entries.answer: The core difference lies in the object, output, and actual authorization: this occupation takes the operation and maintenance and well field and reinjection and compliance and personnel safety of in-service geothermal generating units as its object, and produces operating, maintenance, permit, interconnection, budget, and record results; Industrial Production Managers (11-3051.00) take the output, cost, quality, and personnel management of manufacturing production systems as their object; Quality Control Systems Managers (11-3051.01) take quality systems, inspection, and auditing as their object; Biofuel Production Managers (11-3051.03), Biomass Power Plant Managers (11-3051.04), and Hydroelectric Production Managers (11-3051.06) respectively take their own fuel or hydraulic processes and units as their object; Power Plant Operators (51-8013.00) take operating and monitoring according to procedures as their object and usually work under the direction of a shift supervisor or manager; Geothermal Technicians (49-9099.01) take field testing and maintenance and repair and data collection as their object. Objects and processes differ, and authorization is checked against the actual activities, jurisdiction, and institution, so authority for interconnection negotiation, permit applications, or statutory inspection of pressure and special equipment cannot be carried over from one position to another.

subject.name: Geothermal Production Managers
subject.summary: Geothermal Production Managers corresponds to the exact occupation O*NET/SOC 11-3051.02 'Geothermal Production Managers': manage operations at geothermal power generation facilities, maintain and monitor geothermal plant equipment for efficient and safe plant operations; common job titles include Plant Manager, Plant Supervisor, and Power Plant Operations Manager. Official scope text: Manage operations at geothermal power generation facilities. Maintain and monitor geothermal plant equipment for efficient and safe plant operations. Measure note: the U.S. wages, employment, and industry data presented by O*NET on the 11-3051.02 page are taken from the parent occupation 11-3051.00 (Industrial Production Managers); this page labels them truthfully as parent-occupation measures and does not call them values for this exact occupation itself.
